coverage.headline: Trade Court Judge Mulls Class Cert. For IEEPA Refunds
coverage.summary: A CIT judge did not commit to certifying a class of importers who paid tariffs under Trump's struck-down global tariff regime, though he appeared intrigued by the option during oral argument on the class certification question.

coverage.headline: Biz Pushes Class Cert. As Solution To IEEPA Refund Issues
coverage.summary: A company serving as a test case in the VOS Selections-rooted IEEPA refund litigation argued before the U.S. Court of International Trade that class certification is the appropriate mechanism to resolve refund claims for duties paid under the invalidated global tariff regime.

coverage.headline: To Sue or Not to Sue: That Is the Question for IEEPA Tariff Refunds
coverage.summary: Analysis of the two pending class certification motions in V.O.S. Selections and Freestyle World at the CIT, warning importers with finally-liquidated entries that the two-year statute of limitations under 28 U.S.C. § 1581 is running and that waiting for class certification may permanently foreclose individual recovery rights.

coverage.headline: IEEPA Tariff Refund: Key FAQs for Importers
coverage.summary: BDO's FAQ guide for importers explains the current state of IEEPA tariff refund proceedings stemming from the Supreme Court's ruling in V.O.S. Selections, covering CAPE Phase 1 and 2, class certification motions in the CIT, and the likelihood of further Federal Circuit appeals. Oral arguments on class certification in V.O.S. Selections, Inc. v. United States are noted as scheduled for August 2026, with a CIT ruling expected shortly after.

coverage.headline: CIT Judge Confused By Gov't Objection To Tariff Refund Class
coverage.summary: A U.S. Court of International Trade judge repeatedly expressed confusion over the federal government's objection to certifying a class of importers seeking refunds of President Trump's illegal global IEEPA tariffs. The hearing centered on whether importers with finally liquidated entries should be included in a class action for refund relief in V.O.S. Selections, Inc. v. United States.

coverage.headline: CIT Judge Confused By Gov't Objection To Tariff Refund Class
coverage.summary: A CIT judge repeatedly expressed confusion over the federal government's objection to class certification for importers seeking refunds of Trump's illegal global tariffs, with the VOS brief and government brief both on the record in the proceeding.

coverage.headline: Court of International Trade to Address IEEPA Tariff Refunds in V.O.S. Selections Case
coverage.summary: The Liberty Justice Center announced CIT oral argument on August 6, 2026 on its Rule 23(b)(2) class-certification motion in V.O.S. Selections, seeking to extend CAPE refund access to all importers with finally liquidated entries without requiring each to file a separate lawsuit.

coverage.headline: IEEPA tariff refunds are moving forward
coverage.summary: NRF reports that CBP's CAPE refund system is returning IEEPA tariffs to businesses following the Supreme Court's February 2026 ruling in the consolidated V.O.S. Selections litigation, arguing refunds are pro-worker and pro-growth for retailers and small businesses.

coverage.headline: Beyond CAPE: Importers Move for Class Certification to Recover Liquidated IEEPA Tariffs Not Covered in Phase 1 of Refund Process
coverage.summary: Reports that on June 4, 2026, plaintiffs in V.O.S. Selections filed a Rule 23(b)(2) class certification motion at the CIT on behalf of all importers whose IEEPA refund claims remain ineligible for CAPE processing, a motion that if granted could compel the government to extend CAPE to the entire class across more than 53 million entries and $166 billion in collected duties.
